title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from pp. 39-41: X -> S is a relative curve (hyperbolic, possibly punctured) over a normal base S, with sections xi_i : S -> X, i.e. cusps or marked points. J_i is the ideal of xi_i(S) and J_i/J_i^2 is its conormal line bundle.

Sequence (13) is the homotopy exact sequence of the punctured formal neighbourhood (tubular neighbourhood) of xi_i(S) over S:
 1 -> T -> pi_1(punctured nbhd) -> pi_1(S) -> 1,
with T = Zhat'(1), the tame inertia at the section. Its extension class lies in H^2(S,T). On the previous page Grothendieck asserts that this class is the image of the class of the normal (or conormal) sheaf of X along xi_i under
 Pic(S) -> Pic(S)^ -> H^2(S,T),
the Kummer / l-adic Chern class map (map (18)). In the 'arithmetic' case (S of finite type over Z or Q) this map is injective, because Pic(S) is finitely generated (Mordell-Weil-Neron) and Pic^ embeds in H^2(S,T) via the Kummer sequences.

This page draws the consequences.
(i) In the arithmetic case, (13) splits iff xi_i = 0 in Pic(S). Equivalently, the conormal bundle J_i/J_i^2 is trivial, i.e. there is a global uniformizer of X along xi_i(S). The condition holds Zariski-locally on S, and it is always sufficient for splitting, arithmetic case or not.
(ii) When the bundle is trivial, a choice of basis of J_i/J_i^2 (a 'privileged' uniformizer, i.e. a tangential base point along the section) gives a splitting. The indeterminacy of the basis is G_m(S) = H^0(S,G_m).
(iii) The splittings of (13), up to T-conjugacy, form a torsor under
 H^1(S,T) = lim H^1(S,mu_n)  (20).
(iv) The Kummer sequences 0 -> G_m(S)/n -> H^1(S,mu_n) -> _nPic(S) -> 0 pass to the limit to give
 0 -> G_m(S)^ -> H^1(S,T) -> T(Pic S)  (21),
where T(Pic S) is the Tate module of Pic(S).
(v) In the arithmetic case Pic(S) is finitely generated, so its Tate module vanishes and H^1(S,T) = G_m(S)^.

Conclusion: the full set of splittings ('cuspidal sections' attached to xi_i) is the profinite completion of the set of geometric ones, which come from choices of uniformizer modulo units. This serves the Longue Marche programme: comparing geometric data (sections, tangential base points) with group-theoretic data (sections of fundamental group extensions) over arithmetic bases. It is a relative-over-S version of the section-conjecture analysis at the cusps.
errors: The 'iff' in (i) relies on injectivity of Pic(S) -> H^2(S,T). This holds in the arithmetic case but not in general, as Grothendieck himself notes (only sufficiency is general).
The extension class naturally lives in group cohomology H^2(pi_1(S),T), which maps (injectively) to etale H^2(S,T). Identifying the two is implicit. For H^1 they agree, so (20) is fine.
Sequence (21) is actually also exact on the right: the system G_m(S)/n has surjective transition maps, so lim^1 vanishes (Mittag-Leffler). Grothendieck omits the final -> 0, which is harmless.
'G_m(S)_n' must mean G_m(S)/G_m(S)^n (the cokernel of multiplication by n), not the n-torsion; the transcription is misleading here.

ideas.what: Extension class of the fundamental-group sequence of a punctured tubular neighbourhood of a section equals the Chern (Kummer) class of the normal bundle
ideas.modern_name: l-adic Euler/Chern class of the normal bundle as obstruction to tangential base points; tame fundamental group of a formal neighbourhood of a divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck-Murre (LNM 208, 1971) for the tame formal-neighbourhood theory; topological analogue is classical (Euler class of the circle bundle)
ideas.where_published: Closest is Grothendieck-Murre, The tame fundamental group of a formal neighbourhood of a divisor with normal crossings (LNM 208); the exact statement there is unsure

ideas.what: Splitting iff global uniformizer along the section (trivial conormal bundle); injectivity of Pic -> H^2(S,Zhat(1)) over arithmetic bases via Mordell-Weil-Neron
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points over a base; cuspidal sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Nakamura and others (cuspidal sections)

ideas.what: Splittings form a torsor under H^1(S,Zhat(1)) = G_m(S)^ in the arithmetic case, via limit Kummer sequences; geometric splittings (privileged bases) correspond to G_m(S), dense in the completion
ideas.modern_name: Packets of cuspidal sections parametrized by completed units (Kummer theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Mochizuki; Hoshi; Stix (cuspidal sections over number fields)

missed.claim: A relative-over-S (not just over a field) description of cuspidal sections of the arithmetic fundamental group. The obstruction is the normal-bundle class in Pic(S) -> H^2(S,Zhat(1)), and the parameter space is G_m(S)^ when S is arithmetic. This is a modest, mostly known-in-spirit refinement, written down here in the 1980s.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor of the cuspidal-section packet analysis in anabelian geometry (section conjecture at the cusps) over higher-dimensional arithmetic bases. Its content is largely standard to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean computation that is correct up to minor gaps. It anticipates later treatments of tangential base points and cuspidal-section packets over arithmetic bases, but the ingredients (Kummer theory, Chern class of the normal bundle, finite generation of Pic) are standard. Specialists would find it natural rather than surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'le long de \mathcal{Y}(S)' should be 'le long de \xi_i(S)' (image of the section).
'est une condition[?] au type suffisante' is likely 'est en tout cas suffisante'.
'G_m(S)_n' should be read as G_m(S)/G_m(S)^n, i.e. G_m(S) tensor Z/n.
The last line has the crossed-out G_m before 'H^1(S,T) \simeq G_m(S)^'; the transcription is correct in content.
